correctness.rationale: For fixed peeling depth h≥2, away from negligible root boundary, survival through h rounds equals rooted fringe height≥h. Yule fringe representation with Exp(1) age makes original leaf-child category Poi(a(t)), a=1−e^{−t}, independent of a child branch reaching height≥h−1 by Poisson thinning. This gives exact B_h and Q_h mixture; fixed-size fringe truncation plus bounded differences provides a.s. empirical frequencies. Generation-h expectation ≤t^h/h!, while earliest-child Gamma(h,1) yields B_h≥2^{−h}; splitting ages at h/10 gives TV≤e^{−h/10}+0.1(e/5)^h. Independent quadrature finds B_2≈0.28171808 and rank-one conditional at h=2≈0.53101872, h=12≈0.63029848, corroborating the formulas; no joint n,h limit is asserted.

value.rationale: Leaf proximity and peeling depth are two natural but distinct tree centrality measures. The conditional full leaf-child distribution and sharp asymptotic contrast between unconditional e^{−1} and deep-layer 1−e^{−1} give a meaningful structural dependency, beyond known marginal frequencies.

limitations: Root near-exception fraction tends to zero; rank one interpreted as an original undirected leaf child asymptotically.
Numerical Yule mixture integration at h≤12 is diagnostic, not a general proof.
